title: He wasn’t killed.
paragraphs: He wasn’t killed.
He was betrayed by the boys who called him brother.

Joseph’s coat came back soaked in blood.
His father saw the garment.
And the lie did what lies do best.
It shattered a house.
Genesis 37.
But the real horror was not the torn robe.

It was the envy.
The hatred.
The slow-burning rage that smiled at Joseph one day and sold him the next.

His brothers did not just fake his death.
They buried truth under blood.
They weaponized grief.
They let their father mourn a son who was still breathing.
Sin does that.

It does not only wound the target.
It poisons everyone in the room.
But here’s what we miss…

Genesis 37 is not just about Joseph’s pain.
It is about the human heart without grace.
Jealousy can make family cruel.
Bitterness can make conscience go silent.
And unchecked sin will always demand another lie to keep the first one alive.
Yet even here, God was not absent.

Joseph was in a pit.
Then in chains.
Then in a foreign land.
But never outside the hand of God.

What his brothers meant for evil, God was already bending toward redemption.
Not because evil is good.
But because God is sovereign even over the schemes of broken men.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because Joseph points us to Someone greater.
Jesus was also betrayed.
Not for twenty pieces of silver only—but by the full weight of our sin.
He was stripped.
Rejected.
Handed over.
And unlike Joseph, He truly did die.

But on the third day, Christ rose again so liars, betrayers, the jealous, the bitter, the guilty—
people like us—
could be forgiven and made new.
This story is not only a warning.
It is an invitation.

Bring your hidden envy to Jesus.
Bring your family wounds to Jesus.
Bring the lie you have been protecting to Jesus.

Because the blood of a goat covered a deception.
But the blood of Christ destroys it.

Repent.
Come clean.
There is mercy here.
